newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Ex-Guatemala officials on trial in student's death.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Guatemala officials on trial in student's death.

text.p: In a precedent-setting trial, Guatemala's weak and often ridiculed justice system took on for the first time on Wednesday high government officials accused of responsibility in a killing.

Three criminal court judges began hearing testimony in the trial for the murder of law student Alioto Lopez, 19, who was shot and beaten by anti-riot police during a student protest over a bus fare hike in November 1994.

"It is the first time in the history of Guatemala that high-ranking officials are on trial for violence by security forces," Victor Hugo Villatoro, a student leader who works with the prosecution team, told Reuters in an interview.
Former Interior Minister Danilo Parrinello, his deputy Mario Alfredo Merida, former Police Chief Salvador Figueroa and four police officers are charged with murder in the case.
The ex-minister and his deputy said on Wednesday that they would not testify in the trial.
Villatoro said the prosecution is using a chain-of-command theory to connect the minister and his deputy to the case.
Prosecutors will try to show that officials sent out security forces to calm the days-long riot at the university, but had no control over their subordinates who resorted to indiscriminate violence.
The defence is arguing that the police officers acted in self defence.

Carlos Escobar, a former police officer who appeared in news photos kicking Lopez, took the stand on Wednesday to say that he and fellow police officers were defending themselves against rock-throwing students. Escobar is charged with assassination as well as murder.

Military generals and government ministers have been criminally indicted on accusation of ordering assassinations during the civil war that consumed Guatemala for more than three decades until a peace treaty was signed last year.
But none of them ever stood trial.
Human rights groups and ordinary Guatemalans constantly criticise the justice system for maintaining a tradition of impunity for government and military officials.
For many, the Alioto Lopez murder trial symbolises a break in that tradition.
